provenance: Application-authored original examples calibrated to the paragraph stems and single-best-answer style of MCCQE practice questions 2026. These are not MCC items.

most_likely_diagnosis.vignette: A teenager has abrupt unilateral scrotal pain, vomiting, and an elevated testis with an absent cremasteric reflex.
most_likely_diagnosis.stem: Which diagnosis best explains these findings?

most_likely_diagnosis.vignette: An adult has recurrent vertigo lasting seconds when rolling over in bed, without hearing loss or focal neurologic findings.

differential_diagnosis.vignette: An older adult develops fluctuating inattention over one day during a urinary infection. Their cognition was previously normal.
differential_diagnosis.stem: Which diagnosis best distinguishes this presentation from dementia?

differential_diagnosis.vignette: A child has a barking cough and inspiratory stridor after a viral prodrome, without drooling or a toxic appearance.
differential_diagnosis.stem: Which diagnosis best fits the distinguishing findings?

history_priorities.vignette: A young adult has episodic wheezing that improves on weekends and recurs during shifts at a bakery.
history_priorities.stem: Which additional history would most clarify the cause?
options: Relationship of symptoms to flour exposure

history_priorities.vignette: A patient has presyncope on standing and recently started a new medication for urinary symptoms.
history_priorities.stem: Which history detail is most useful diagnostically?
options: Timing of symptoms relative to starting the medication

physical_exam_interpretation.vignette: An adult with breathlessness has unilateral reduced breath sounds, reduced chest expansion, and stony dullness to percussion at the right base.
physical_exam_interpretation.stem: What do these examination findings most strongly suggest?

physical_exam_interpretation.vignette: A patient with leg swelling has elevated jugular venous pressure that increases with abdominal pressure.
physical_exam_interpretation.stem: What does this finding most strongly indicate?

diagnostic_investigation.vignette: A stable adult has progressive solid-food dysphagia and unintentional weight loss over several months.
diagnostic_investigation.stem: Which investigation is most appropriate to establish the diagnosis?

diagnostic_investigation.vignette: A nonpregnant adult has polyuria and polydipsia without acute illness or previously measured blood glucose.
diagnostic_investigation.stem: Which investigation most directly evaluates the suspected diagnosis?

laboratory_interpretation.vignette: An adult with fatigue has hemoglobin 94 g/L, mean corpuscular volume 70 fL, ferritin 6 micrograms/L, and an elevated total iron-binding capacity.
laboratory_interpretation.stem: Which interpretation best fits these laboratory findings?

laboratory_interpretation.vignette: A patient has pH 7.28, bicarbonate 14 mmol/L, and sodium 140 and chloride 103 mmol/L.
laboratory_interpretation.stem: What is the primary acid-base disturbance?

imaging_interpretation.vignette: After a fall, an older adult has hip pain. Radiographs show a fracture line through the femoral neck, proximal to the greater and lesser trochanters.
imaging_interpretation.stem: Which fracture location is shown by this description?

imaging_interpretation.vignette: An adult has sudden pleuritic pain. Chest radiography shows a visible visceral pleural line with no lung markings peripheral to it.
imaging_interpretation.stem: What does this radiographic finding indicate?

ecg_interpretation.vignette: An adult with palpitations has an ECG showing an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm at 130/min, without discrete P waves.
An asymptomatic adult has a regular ECG at 70/min with a P wave before each QRS and a constant PR interval of 240 ms.

diagnostic_criteria.vignette: An adult has depressed mood, anhedonia, insomnia, low energy, poor concentration, guilt, and impaired function daily for three weeks, without mania or substance exposure.
diagnostic_criteria.stem: Which diagnosis is supported by the symptom duration and number?

diagnostic_criteria.vignette: An adult has excessive difficult-to-control worry across several domains with restlessness, fatigue, poor concentration, and sleep disturbance for eight months.
diagnostic_criteria.stem: Which disorder is supported by these diagnostic features?

risk_stratification.vignette: An adult has suspected upper gastrointestinal bleeding with systolic pressure 85 mm Hg, tachycardia, and syncope.
risk_stratification.stem: How should the immediate clinical risk be classified?
options: High risk because of hemodynamic instability
Low risk because bleeding is unconfirmed
Low risk because age is unspecified

risk_stratification.vignette: A postoperative patient has new dyspnea, unilateral leg swelling, tachycardia, and no more likely alternative diagnosis.
risk_stratification.stem: How do these findings affect the pretest probability of pulmonary embolism?

evidence_statistical_interpretation.vignette: Among 100 patients with disease, a test is positive in 90. Among 100 patients without disease, it is negative in 80.
evidence_statistical_interpretation.stem: What is the sensitivity of this test?

evidence_statistical_interpretation.vignette: A trial finds an outcome in 10% of treated participants and 15% of controls over two years.
evidence_statistical_interpretation.stem: What is the absolute risk reduction over two years?

initial_stabilization.vignette: After eating nuts, an adult has wheezing, generalized urticaria, and blood pressure 75/40 mm Hg.
initial_stabilization.stem: Which immediate treatment is most appropriate?

initial_stabilization.vignette: A newborn remains apneic with a heart rate of 80/min after warming, positioning, drying, and stimulation.

treatment_choice.vignette: A healthy nonpregnant adult has uncomplicated cystitis without fever or flank pain and with normal renal function.
An adult has a first episode of a mild depressive illness and prefers a psychological treatment. There is no suicidality or psychosis.
treatment_choice.stem: Which treatment is a reasonable initial choice?
options: Electroconvulsive therapy as the only choice

pharmacology_contraindications.vignette: A patient taking sildenafil asks about using nitroglycerin for chest discomfort.
pharmacology_contraindications.stem: Which adverse interaction is most concerning?

pharmacology_contraindications.vignette: A pregnant patient at ten weeks takes an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor for hypertension.
pharmacology_contraindications.stem: Which medication requires replacement because of fetal risk?

procedural_intervention.vignette: An adult has a fluctuant cutaneous abscess with surrounding tenderness and no systemic instability.
A patient has fever and an obstructing ureteral stone with hydronephrosis despite initial antibiotics and resuscitation.
procedural_intervention.stem: Which intervention is needed for source control?

long_term_management.vignette: An adult with persistent asthma uses a reliever frequently and has recurrent night symptoms over several months.
long_term_management.stem: Which ongoing strategy best addresses airway inflammation?

long_term_management.vignette: An adult with stable opioid use disorder requests maintenance treatment and has no contraindications.
long_term_management.stem: Which ongoing treatment can reduce overdose risk?

follow_up_monitoring.vignette: An adult starts an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor for hypertension and has stable baseline kidney function.
follow_up_monitoring.stem: Which laboratory values should be reassessed after initiation?

follow_up_monitoring.vignette: A patient starts lithium for bipolar disorder and returns for planned medication monitoring.
follow_up_monitoring.stem: Which measurement is essential to guide safe dosing?

disposition_escalation.vignette: A young infant has fever, poor feeding, lethargy, and delayed capillary refill in a community clinic.
options: Return only if a rash develops

disposition_escalation.vignette: An adult with depression describes a specific suicide plan, access to the means, and inability to remain safe at home.
disposition_escalation.stem: Which level of care is most appropriate now?

patient_counselling.vignette: A patient newly diagnosed with hypertension asks why treatment matters when they feel well.
options: Treatment lowers future stroke and heart disease risk even without symptoms.
You need treatment only when you feel a headache.
Feeling well proves there is no risk.
Medication guarantees you will never have a stroke.
Blood pressure has no effect on kidney health.

patient_counselling.vignette: A parent asks whether antibiotics will help a child with an uncomplicated viral upper respiratory infection.
options: Antibiotics do not treat viruses, and we can discuss symptom relief and warning signs.
There is no need to discuss warning signs.
The infection will always persist without antibiotics.

informed_consent_discussion.vignette: A competent patient is considering elective surgery and asks what they should understand before deciding.
informed_consent_discussion.stem: Which discussion best supports informed consent?
options: Discuss benefits, material risks, alternatives, and the option of no treatment.
Ask for a signature before answering questions.
Describe only rare risks unrelated to the choice.
Ask the family to decide without involving the patient.

informed_consent_discussion.vignette: A patient is offered a medication with two reasonable alternatives and wants help understanding the choice.
informed_consent_discussion.stem: Which response best supports an informed decision?
options: Explain the expected benefits, relevant harms, and alternatives in understandable terms.
Say that questions will delay treatment unnecessarily.
Present a consent form without explanation.
Discuss only the most expensive alternative.

shared_decision_making.vignette: Two treatments offer similar clinical benefit but differ in recovery time. The patient is a caregiver and worries about time away from home.
shared_decision_making.stem: Which response best supports shared decision-making?
options: Ask how recovery demands fit the patient’s priorities and compare the options together.
Choose without discussing the patient’s priorities.
Assume all caregivers prefer the shortest procedure.
Ask the family to decide in the patient’s absence.

shared_decision_making.vignette: An adult eligible for a screening intervention wants to weigh its benefits against false-positive results.
shared_decision_making.stem: Which response best supports a shared choice?
options: Discuss likely benefits and harms and ask what matters most to the patient.
State that everyone must make the same choice.
Ask for agreement before explaining the options.
Provide only a technical guideline without discussion.

difficult_news.vignette: A patient has just learned that biopsy results show cancer and becomes silent and tearful.
options: I can see this is a lot to take in. What is going through your mind?
There is no reason to be upset.
Let us finish the paperwork first.
You should focus only on being positive.
Everyone reacts this way, so let us move on.

difficult_news.vignette: A parent is told that their child has a serious chronic illness and asks for a moment.
options: Take the time you need. I will stay here and answer questions when you are ready.
We must finish all details immediately.
You should have expected this result.

health_literacy.vignette: A patient nods during instructions for a new inhaler but appears unsure how to use it.
options: Please show me how you will use the inhaler so I can check how clearly I explained it.
Read the technical manual before asking questions.
Your nod means the instructions are clear.
Ask someone else to explain it later.

health_literacy.vignette: A patient with limited English proficiency needs to discuss a new diagnosis, and a young child offers to translate.
health_literacy.stem: Which communication strategy is most appropriate?
options: Ask the child to interpret all sensitive information.
Assume written English instructions are sufficient.

treatment_barriers.vignette: A patient with diabetes has missed several doses and says food and rent costs have increased.
treatment_barriers.stem: Which response best explores the treatment barrier?
options: Can we talk about the cost of your medicines and what options might make them easier to obtain?
You must choose medicines instead of food.
I will assume you no longer want treatment.
There are no alternatives worth discussing.

treatment_barriers.vignette: A patient misses appointments and explains that bus service was cut in their neighbourhood.
options: Let us explore transport or appointment options that could work for you.
Missing visits proves you do not value your health.
I will stop care without discussion.
Transport cannot affect access to care.

ethics.vignette: A capable adult declines a recommended transfusion after understanding its risks, benefits, and alternatives.
ethics.stem: Which ethical principle most directly supports respecting this refusal?

ethics.vignette: Two patients have equal clinical need for a scarce resource and no relevant prognostic difference.
ethics.stem: Which allocation approach is ethically preferable?
options: Use a transparent, fair process based on relevant criteria.
Choose according to personal approval of lifestyle.

confidentiality.vignette: An adult patient’s employer requests diagnostic details without consent or a legal requirement for disclosure.
confidentiality.stem: Which professional action is most appropriate?
options: Seek the patient’s consent before releasing relevant information.
Disclose details to any manager who asks.
Post the diagnosis in a workplace notice.

confidentiality.vignette: A capable adult asks that their diagnosis not be shared with a relative who calls the clinic. There is no applicable exception to confidentiality.
options: Maintain confidentiality and discuss consent with the patient if needed.
Release the chart because the caller is family.
Confirm all details over the telephone.
Ask reception to share the diagnosis.
Assume all relatives are substitute decision-makers.

capacity_consent.vignette: An adult refuses surgery but can understand the information, appreciate the consequences, reason about the options, and communicate a choice.
options: Disagreement alone does not establish incapacity.
The surgeon becomes the substitute decision-maker.
A family objection overrides the capable patient.

capacity_consent.vignette: A patient with a dementia diagnosis accurately explains a proposed simple treatment, its consequences, and their consistent choice.
capacity_consent.stem: Which statement about capacity is most appropriate?
options: Capacity is decision-specific and cannot be inferred solely from the diagnosis.
Dementia always removes capacity for every decision.
Capacity requires agreeing with the physician.

professional_boundaries.vignette: A physician is asked to prescribe long-term controlled medication to a close friend outside a therapeutic relationship.
professional_boundaries.stem: Which action best maintains professional boundaries?
options: Arrange independent clinical assessment through an appropriate treating clinician.
Accept a gift in exchange for prescribing.
Document the prescription only in a personal notebook.

professional_boundaries.vignette: A current patient asks their physician to begin a romantic relationship.
professional_boundaries.stem: Which professional response is most appropriate?
options: Maintain the professional boundary and decline the relationship.
Accept if the patient initiates it.

patient_safety.vignette: A clinic discovers that two patients have similar names and a medication order was nearly placed in the wrong chart.
options: Use reliable patient identifiers and review the ordering workflow.
Blame the patient with the more common name.
Remove all identification checks to speed care.

patient_safety.vignette: A ward identifies repeated medication omissions during shift handover.
patient_safety.stem: Which response best addresses the system risk?
options: Review the handover process and implement a reliable medication reconciliation check.
Tell staff to be more careful without examining the process.
Assume no harm means no action is needed.

error_disclosure.vignette: A patient receives the wrong medication dose because of an ordering error. They are stable after immediate assessment.
error_disclosure.stem: Which professional action is required next?
options: Disclose the error promptly and explain known facts and the care plan.
Wait for the patient to discover the error.
Change the record to conceal the dose.
Blame an absent colleague without investigation.
Disclose only if permanent harm occurs.

error_disclosure.vignette: A clinician discovers that a diagnostic result was overlooked and treatment was delayed.
error_disclosure.stem: Which action best meets the duty of disclosure?
options: Inform the patient promptly about known facts, consequences, and next steps.
Avoid discussion because the delay has ended.
Ask the patient to waive their right to information.

canadian_obligations.vignette: A Canadian physician has reasonable grounds to suspect that a child is being abused. No immediate threat to the physician prevents action.
options: Report the concern to the appropriate child-protection authority under applicable law.
Wait until abuse is proven in court.
Require parental permission before any report.
Delegate the entire duty to the suspected abuser.

canadian_obligations.vignette: A physician is unsure whether a provincial reporting law applies to a specific patient situation. The patient is currently safe.
canadian_obligations.stem: Which professional action is most appropriate?
options: Clarify the applicable provincial duty using authoritative guidance and act accordingly.
Assume every province has identical rules.
Ask an unrelated patient to interpret the law.
